clue.text: Buys tea in bags

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the drink goes inside the word for bags

blocks.note: purses are small bags
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone shopping for tea sold in teabags.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha (also char) is an informal British word for tea, from Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: To purchase is to buy, and the third-person verb form matches 'buys'.

clue.text: Up mountain, two sharp bends and a square

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: an Alp is a mountain
the letter Z is drawn with two sharp turns
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountain road climbing through a pair of hairpin bends to a village square.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter Z is pictured by its shape: a line that zigzags with two sharp corners.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square in a town, a word borrowed from Spanish.

clue.text: Animal came ‘ither by boat, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken version, so the spelling may differ

blocks.note: came hither by boat is rowed here, said with dropped h's as the apostrophe in 'ither suggests

explanation.surface: A dialect speaker describing an animal arriving by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped h of 'ither tells you to drop the h of here too, so 'rowed 'ere' matches roe deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small deer of Europe and Asia, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Twitcher’s refuge is somewhat ghastly

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the word is used, so its end is cut away

blocks.note: hideous means ghastly

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher complains that the shelter is pretty grim.
explanation.walkthrough: Part of HIDEOUS is kept, dropping the final OUS. A twitcher is a keen birdwatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is a camouflaged shelter from which birdwatchers observe birds unseen.

clue.text: Top Surrey cricketers out with boat

indicators.note: the top of each word is its first letter, so only the initials are taken

blocks.note: initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: The best Surrey cricket team has been dismissed, alongside a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top Surrey cricketers' reads as the county's best players, but Top takes the first letter of each of the next four words.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat used for carrying freight.

clue.text: Light clothing from Asia. Fruits served

indicators.note: food that is served is prepared and dished up, so the letters are made over into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Lightweight clothes come from Asia, and then fruit is brought to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The full stop splits the surface into two sentences, but the fodder runs across it.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari suit is a lightweight belted jacket and trousers, worn in hot climates.

clue.text: Suffer backing old police force and its patch

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police until 2001
the force's territory was Northern Ireland, NI

explanation.surface: Supporting a former police force and the area it covered.
explanation.walkthrough: RUC followed by NI, all written backwards, gives INCUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to suffer it or bring it upon yourself.

clue.text: Part of engine congested with dirt

indicators.note: something congested is clogged and jumbled up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A component of a motor clogged up with grime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of engine' looks like a hidden-word instruction, but Part alone is the definition; 'with' joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one component or element of a mixture or whole.

clue.text: Amusing character, one with a couple of females. That’s capital!

blocks.note: a card is a funny, eccentric person
Roman numeral for one
F for female, twice

explanation.surface: A joker with two women in tow, and someone exclaims how splendid it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's capital!' sounds like old-fashioned praise, but capital is the definition: a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: Sympathetic sound conveyed on a screen

indicators.note: conveyed suggests things carried and moved about, so the letters shift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A caring tone delivered through a monitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Sympathetic here is the physics sense: sympathetic vibration is one body vibrating in response to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonance is sound produced when one body vibrates in sympathy with another at the same frequency.

clue.text: Mathematical ability required when holding Chippendales auditions?

blocks.note: first meaning: a talent for numbers
second, playful meaning: a boss who judges bodies

explanation.surface: Being good at sums is needed to run the try-outs for a male striptease troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chippendales are a male striptease troupe; their auditions need someone in charge, a head, to assess physiques, or figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a head for figures is the idiom for being good at arithmetic and numbers.

clue.text: A truly incomplete state

indicators.note: incomplete means the word is missing its last part, so its final letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
very in its old sense of true, as in 'the very truth'

explanation.surface: A country or condition that is not quite whole.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a noun, a nation, but it is the verb: to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare something firmly, which is to state it.

clue.text: Chips in, holding a dairy cow

indicators.note: something holding another wraps around it, so the single letter goes inside

blocks.note: chips are fries in American usage
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fried potatoes go in, and a milking cow is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: Chips are British fried potato sticks, what Americans call fries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Friesian is a black-and-white breed of cattle kept for its high milk yield.

clue.text: Crimson first lady prunes blossoms again

blocks.note: crimson is a shade of red
Eve, the first woman in the Bible
to lop is to cut off branches

explanation.surface: A gardener in red cuts back plants that then flower a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife, but here it is the Bible's first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop is to grow or unfold, like a bloom; redevelops is doing so a second time.

clue.text: Nuneaton’s alter ago, we hear!

definitions.note: a play on alter ego: the answer is a second identity for the sounded phrase

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken version, so the town's name counts by its sound

blocks.note: the town's name said aloud is like 'none eaten', which the answer restates

explanation.surface: A joke about the alter ego of the English town of Nuneaton.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuneaton is a town in Warwickshire. Spoken, it suggests 'none eaten', and the answer is a synonym, a second self for the phrase; 'alter ago' plays on alter ego.
explanation.definitionFit: Food left uneaten has not been consumed, so the word fits 'none eaten'.

clue.text: Officers giving material to the workers

blocks.note: serge is a hard-wearing woollen fabric
worker ants: the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Managers handing cloth out to the factory staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeants are non-commissioned officers in the army or police.

clue.text: Turned round, getting different views seeing valley going north

indicators.note: different means changed, so these letters are put in another order
in a down clue, heading north means reading upwards, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a dell is a small wooded valley

explanation.surface: Someone turning to admire changing views of a valley as they head north.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel is to rotate on a pivot, so swivelled means turned round.

clue.text: Pub containing four regularly having a joke

indicators.note: containing means the pub's word wraps around the other letters
regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
first and third letters

explanation.surface: A group of four in a bar sharing a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something in fun means saying it as a joke, not seriously, so the phrase means joking.

clue.text: Peaceful girl, alluring one, topless, at end of promenade

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, which in this across clue is the first letter
the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a siren is a seductive woman
final letter

explanation.surface: A seductive young woman, scantily clad, at the end of the seafront.
explanation.walkthrough: The name Irene comes from the Greek for peace, hence 'peaceful girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a girl's name from Eirene, the Greek goddess and word for peace.

clue.text: Money paid out to former US vice-president, we’re told

indicators.note: being told something is hearing it said, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: ex- means former
Mike Pence, US vice-president 2017 to 2021

explanation.surface: Cash handed over to a past American vice-president.
explanation.walkthrough: Ex-Pence, the former vice-president, said aloud matches the answer; pence also suits a clue about money.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense is money spent or a cost incurred, so it is money paid out.

clue.text: Align oneself round gallery, admitting it’s nothing in Nancy

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so the French word goes inside

blocks.note: a round shape, the letter O
French for nothing; Nancy is a city in France
the Tate gallery in London

explanation.surface: Getting your bearings around an art gallery, with nothing much to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy is the French city, not a woman's name, so the word for nothing is French. The Tate is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate is to find your position or bearings, aligning yourself relative to surroundings.

clue.text: Minerva regularly gripped by desire to win

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one
gripped by means held inside the next word

blocks.note: to ache for is to desire
second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: The goddess Minerva repeatedly seized by a will to triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desire to win' looks like one phrase; the definition is just win, with to as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve is to succeed in gaining something, so it means to win.

clue.text: Bridge opponents from the media love coffee

blocks.note: in bridge East and South are on opposing sides
the press, newspapers
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Card players and journalists sharing a passion for coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is the card game, where partners sit North-South and East-West, so East and South are rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Down-at-heel old solver given hiding!

indicators.note: hiding means the answer is concealed inside the clue's own letters

blocks.note: found across 'at-heel'

explanation.surface: A shabby elderly crossword fan is given a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: A hiding is a thrashing in the surface. The solver is the person the clue addresses: you, in old form.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is the archaic form of 'you', the person addressed, here the solver.

clue.text: Stops blowing top and relaxes

indicators.note: losing the top, in a down clue, means removing the first letter

blocks.note: to cease is to stop

explanation.surface: Someone stops losing their temper and calms down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing top' reads as getting angry, but it means dropping the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to loosen or lessen tension, so eases matches relaxes.

clue.text: Buffoons regularly, little green men seen here?

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Clowns keep showing up; perhaps aliens have landed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a description by example: aliens are said to travel in flying saucers.
explanation.definitionFit: UFOs, unidentified flying objects, are where popular culture places little green aliens.

clue.text: Emperor ran away from Italian city

indicators.note: away from means removed out of the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
Otranto, a port in southern Italy

explanation.surface: A ruler fled an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ran looks like the verb of escape; it is the three letters taken out of OTRANTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto the Great and later Ottos were Holy Roman Emperors.

clue.text: Anthem offering trade-offs with hymnal, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A national song that might come in a hymn book along with some compromises.
explanation.definitionFit: Land of My Fathers is the English title of the Welsh national anthem, Hen Wlad Fy Nhadau.

clue.text: Conferences on limiting food?

blocks.note: first meaning: formal assemblies, as in the Diet of Worms
second meaning: eating plans that restrict what you eat

explanation.surface: Meetings held about cutting back what we eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A diet is also a legislative assembly, as in the Japanese Diet or the Diet of Worms, a 1521 meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Diets are both formal assemblies and regimes that restrict eating, two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: Comes across record deliveries

blocks.note: a disc is a gramophone record
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries

explanation.surface: Someone finds a record of parcels sent out.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliveries are balls bowled in cricket; six make an over.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to find it, often by chance, so it means to come across it.
